plain_english: You don't understand this. You wear an expression that doesn't match your real situation. You're like people who sit in the circus or theater, not knowing their house is already burning down. But I can see from up high what storms are coming for you. They will either hit you later like a flood, or they're already close and about to sweep away everything you own. Even though you barely notice it, isn't there a spinning hurricane right now confusing your mind? It makes you chase after things, then run from the same things. It lifts you up one moment, then crashes you down the next.
original_excerpt: This you do not understand, and you bear a countenance which does not befit your condition, like many men who sit in the circus or the theatre without having learned that their home is already in mourning: but I, looking forward from a lofty standpoint, can see what storms are either threatening you, and will burst in torrents upon you somewhat later, or are close upon you and on the point of sweeping away all that you possess. Why, though you are hardly aware of it, is there not a whirling hurricane at this moment spinning round and confusing your minds, making them seek and avoid the very same things, now raising them aloft and now dashing them below? . . . . . .”
